title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Materials and methods · abstract-2-1】This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p < 0.001). Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed distinct immune and proliferative patterns consistent with model predictions.
